blocks.text: What a Top-Scrub and Recoat Actually Includes

A top-scrub and recoat, sometimes called scrub-and-recoat or deep scrub, removes the soiled upper layers of floor finish without stripping to bare tile. The crew dust mops, applies a neutral or mildly alkaline scrub solution, scrubs with a red or blue pad on a rotary machine or a compact scrubber-dryer, recovers the slurry, rinses, and lays two to three fresh coats of finish. Because the base layers remain intact, the job uses less chemistry, less water, and roughly half the labor of a full strip.

That labor difference is why unit pricing sits well below strip-and-wax rates. Where a full strip averages $0.30 to $0.60 per sq ft, a top-scrub and recoat usually runs $0.12 to $0.30. It is the workhorse service in most deep floor programs, scheduled quarterly or semiannually to keep gloss up and push full strips out to every 18 to 36 months.

Vendors quote this service three ways: a per-sq-ft rate, an hourly specialty rate, or a flat job price that is really a disguised per-sq-ft rate with a minimum. The table below converts all three into comparable numbers using a two-person crew that scrubs and recoats 1,200 to 1,800 sq ft per crew-hour on open floors.

blocks.title: Quick sanity check
blocks.text: If a quote for an open, lightly furnished floor exceeds $0.30 per sq ft for scrub-and-recoat, ask whether the vendor actually priced a full strip. If it falls below $0.10 on a small floor, confirm the coat count; one thin coat of finish is a spray buff, not a recoat.

Hourly billing at $55 to $95 per technician hour appears most often for small or irregular jobs: a kitchenette, a copy room, or a lobby with many edges. It is fair when the scope is hard to measure, but it shifts productivity risk to you. Per-sq-ft billing is better for corridors and open areas because you know the total in advance and can compare bidders directly.

To convert an hourly quote, multiply the estimated hours by the rate and divide by VCT square footage. A quote of two technicians for four hours at $65 per hour on 2,000 sq ft equals $520, or $0.26 per sq ft, which is within range for that size. If the vendor says six hours instead, the effective rate jumps to $0.39, a signal to ask why.

Minimums of $200 to $400 cover mobilization: loading a scrubber, finish, pads, wet vacuum, and cones, plus travel and setup. Routine janitorial visits carry their own per-visit minimum of roughly $90 to $135, but floor care minimums run higher because of equipment and the two-person crew. If you have only 600 sq ft of VCT, you will pay the minimum regardless. Pairing that small job with carpet extraction or another periodic task on the same night is the best way to spread mobilization cost.
Factors That Push the Unit Price Up or Down

items: Equipment fit: a 17-inch cordless scrubber-dryer with a 6-gallon tank speeds open corridors, while tight offices need a rotary machine and hand edging.
Finish condition: floors recoated on schedule need one light scrub pass; neglected floors may need a deeper scrub or a full strip.
Coat count: two coats is standard; three coats add roughly 15 to 20 percent to material and labor.
Access windows: weekend-only or after-midnight work adds 8 to 15 percent for differentials.
Daily care quality: dust mopping, mechanical sweeping, and neutral damp mopping reduce grit that dulls finish between recoats.
Volume bundling: adding scrub-and-recoat to a quarterly deep floor program typically trims the rate 5 to 10 percent.

blocks.text: Most offices fold scrub-and-recoat into a deep floor program amortized at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month. Here is how the math works for 6,000 sq ft of VCT recoated quarterly at $0.18 per sq ft: $1,080 per visit times four visits equals $4,320 per year, or $360 per month, which is $0.06 per sq ft of VCT per month. If the floor is only recoated twice a year, the monthly equivalent falls to $180, or $0.03 per sq ft.

items.name: Measure VCT only
items.text: Exclude carpet, ceramic tile, and polished concrete from the scrub-and-recoat square footage.

items.name: Pick a frequency
items.text: Quarterly for moderate traffic, semiannual for light traffic, monthly or bimonthly for heavy entry lanes.

items.name: Apply the rate
items.text: Use $0.12 to $0.30 per sq ft based on area and obstacles, checking for minimum charges.

items.name: Annualize and amortize
items.text: Multiply by visits per year and divide by 12 to compare against monthly deep floor program quotes.

blocks.title: Safety and specs to require
blocks.text: Ask for Safety Data Sheets for scrub solution and finish under OSHA HazCom, a certificate of insurance, and proper coning while floors are wet. If sustainability matters, request Green Seal certified finishes and confirm slurry disposal follows local wastewater rules.

Between visits, a quiet dual-rotor mechanical sweeper handles daytime lobby grit without cords or noise, and an 18-inch squeegee kit keeps glass entry doors clear so staff are not tracking residue from wiped-down sidelights onto fresh finish. These small practices extend recoat intervals.

faqs.q: What is a typical VCT top-scrub and recoat unit price?
faqs.a: Most US offices pay $0.12 to $0.30 per sq ft of VCT per visit. Large open floors over 10,000 sq ft trend toward $0.12 to $0.18, mid-size areas toward $0.15 to $0.24, and small or obstructed spaces toward $0.22 to $0.30 or the job minimum of $200 to $400.

faqs.q: How is scrub-and-recoat different from a full strip and wax?
faqs.a: Scrub-and-recoat removes only the soiled top layers of finish and adds two to three new coats, while a full strip removes all finish down to bare tile and applies four to six coats. Scrub-and-recoat costs roughly 40 to 60 percent of a strip and takes about half the labor and cure time.

faqs.q: Is hourly or per-sq-ft billing better for floor recoating?
faqs.a: Per-sq-ft billing is better for open corridors and large areas because the total is fixed and easy to compare. Hourly billing at $55 to $95 per technician hour can be reasonable for small, irregular rooms, but ask for a not-to-exceed cap so productivity risk does not fall entirely on you.

faqs.q: How do I convert a scrub-and-recoat schedule into a monthly budget?
faqs.a: Multiply VCT square footage by the per-visit rate, multiply by visits per year, and divide by 12. For example, 6,000 sq ft at $0.18 quarterly equals $360 per month. When combining with routine cleaning, routine visits per month use 4.333 weeks per month, while periodic floor care is amortized separately.

faqs.q: What should be in the contract for a scrub-and-recoat program?
faqs.a: List VCT square footage, frequency, pad type, number of finish coats, finish solids content, access hours, and furniture-moving responsibility. Require a certificate of insurance, OSHA HazCom Safety Data Sheets, and a dated work log so you can verify each visit against invoices.
